chunks: Al-Tatari narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Alaa ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the people of Medina said to me, 'O Abu Ja'far, why do I not see you performing voluntary prayer between the call to prayer (adhan) and the proclamation for prayer (iqamah), as people do?' He said, 'I said to him: When we intend to perform voluntary prayer, our voluntary prayer is performed at a time other than the time of the obligatory prayer. So when the obligatory prayer enters, there is no voluntary prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Why do Shia Muslims not pray voluntary prayer between the Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Shia practice of withholding voluntary prayer (nafl) between the adhan and iqamah stems from the principle that the specific time for the obligatory prayer (fard) is reserved exclusively for it, preventing the mixing of distinct worship periods. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the interval between call and proclamation is part of the fard's temporal domain, unlike the Sunni practice of offering sunnah prayers during this window, thereby emphasizing the purity and distinctness of the obligatory act.
